headline: Continued seven applications, including 270 Loudon Road, to October 21; adopted new parking, loading, and driveway rules.
summary: Granted a driveway permit on Sanders Street and a lot line adjustment on Hoit Road, and approved a pylon sign at 30 Manchester Street. Adopted changes to site plan rules for parking, loading, driveways, and lighting. Seven items, including 270 Loudon Road and 94-98 Manchester Street, were continued to October 21, 2026.
decisions: Approved the August 19, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 7-0.
Continued the 110-unit multifamily building at 270 Loudon Road to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the 4-story building at 94-98 Manchester Street to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the 2-unit condominium conversion at 3 Palm Street to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the car dealership project at 110 Manchester Street to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the 24-lot subdivision off Mooreland Avenue to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the second driveway at 27 Hobart Street to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Continued the second driveway at 109-109.5 Warren Street to October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Approved seven sign design reviews on the consent agenda, items 5A through 5G, 7-0.
Determined the micro-data center application at 52 Locke Road complete and set a public hearing for October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Determined the St. Paul's School mail center application at 7 Rectory Road complete and set a public hearing for October 21, 2026, 7-0.
Approved the revised signs for Yamas Greek Eatery at 25 South Main Street, 7-0.
Approved the zoning-compliant P1 pylon sign at 30 Manchester Street with conditions, 7-0; all other signs return October 21, 2026.
Adopted amendments to Site Plan Regulations Sections 18, 19, 20, and 29, effective when City Council adopts related zoning changes, 7-0.
Determined the Sanders Street driveway application complete and opened the public hearing, 7-0.
Granted conditional use permit approval for a driveway about 65 feet from the Sanders and Merrimack Streets intersection, 7-0, with conditions.
Determined the Hoit Road lot line adjustment application complete and opened the public hearing, 7-0.
Granted four subdivision waiver requests for the 109 Hoit Road lot line adjustment, 7-0.
Granted conditional minor subdivision approval for the lot line adjustment at 109 Hoit Road, 7-0, subject to conditions.
Withdrawn: the 2-lot minor subdivision at 61 Mountain Rd was withdrawn at the applicant's request.
Directed staff to tell Hopkinton the City has no particular objections or comments at this time on the 8-lot subdivision.

Gateway Performance (GWP District. (PL-ADR-2026-0199) (2026-079) 
 
Mr. Bass noted this application involves a master sign plan for a significant multi-tenant commercial 
development at 30 Manchester Street. Mr. Bass explained that when the site's major site plan was 
previously approved, tenancy was unknown. The applicant has prepared a master sign plan for all 
known signs with the master sign plan with the exception of the car wash as the tenancy is still 
unknown. The Architectural Design Review Committee reviewed the full master sign plan and 
provided recommended conditions of approval with the understanding that the master sign plan as it 
is non-conforming with zoning. The applicant has taken an excerpt of that master sign plan and 
created a zoning compliant package that they brought before Architectural Design Review 
Committee. They request to move forward with certain signage that are within the master sign plan. 
Mr. Bass noted some of the signs have been determined that they need conditional use permit 
applications and other items. For this hearing, the Board is being asked to approve the free-standing 
pylon sign. There is an element of the pylon sign they are proposing an electronic messaging sign in 
their master sign plan and that is non-conforming with zoning. In the zoning compliant package, they 
have removed the electronic messaging. If the Board is willing to approve the zoning compliant 
package so if they do receive the zoning relief they can slide that in and everything else comes back 
to the Board.    
 
Jason Gagnon (225 E Industrial Park Dr, Manchester) and Brad Pernoff from The Common Man. Mr. 
Gagnon explained that the full master sign plan including the majority of wall signs is headed to the 
Zoning Board of Adjustment on October 7th, and those signs requiring conditional use permits will 
return to the Planning Board on October 21st for the wall signs. Mr. Gagnon noted the code compliant 
package the focus is on the freestanding pylon sign (P1), noting that the electronic message center 
(EMC) component shown in the master sign plan had been removed from the zoning-compliant 
submission and replaced with a manual changeable copy board. Mr. Gagnon noted the electronic 
messaging signs are prohibited under the current zoning ordinance. Mr. Gagnon noted that sign 
cabinet backgrounds have been changed to an opaque beige/ivory color, consistent with an approach 
previously used at a Manchester location.

other signs shall return to the October 21, 2026 Planning Board meeting for final approval. 
 
8. Public Hearings 
8A. Public Hearing for the Planning Board to consider adoption of amendments to the Site Plan 
Regulations: amending Section 18 (Parking Lot Design Standards), Section 19 (Access and Driveway 
Standards), Section 20 (Loading and Solid Waste Facility Standards), and Section 29 (Lighting).
City of Concord Planning Board 
September 16, 2026 
 Minutes 
 
 
6 
 
 
 
Mr. Thompson stated staff is recommending the Board approve the proposed amendments to the Site 
Plan Regulations, to be effective upon the City Council adopting related Zoning Ordinance 
Amendments, which are scheduled for public hearing on October 13.  This amendment effort follows 
a robust review of regulatory requirements surrounding parking (including at least a dozen drafts and 
iterations of proposed regulatory changes), and a collaborative process with many Community 
Development Department staff members.  Through this effort, staff has coalesced around the proposal 
now being presented to the Planning Board, focusing on mechanisms for relief from the regulatory 
standards as an interim step, understanding that wholesale policy changes are best suited for 
development following the completion of the Master Plan process, which is now underway.   If 
adopted, these amendments will provide significantly increased flexibility for relief from the 
regulatory requirements associated with parking, loading, and driveway access.  The shift of the 
majority of design standards to the Site Plan Regulations allows the use of waivers, a less stringent 
statutory standard of relief, administered by the Planning Board, eliminating most of the need to seek 
variance relief from the Zoning Board of Adjustment.  For the minority of projects that do not require 
site plan review, the related Zoning Ordinance amendments will create conditional use permit relief 
valves, again putting administration of relief in the hands of the Planning Board rather than the 
ZBA.  Lastly, these regulation amendments (in conjunction with the related Zoning amendments) 
eliminate the challenges associated with differing standards that exist today between the regulations 
and Zoning Ordinance. 
 
Chair Woodfin opened the public hearing, after receiving no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed 
the public hearing.  
 
On a motion made by Chair Woodfin, seconded by Member Rosenberger, the Board voted 7-0-0 to 
adopt the proposed Site Plan Regulation Amendments to Sections 18, 19, 20, and 29, effective upon 
the City Council's adoption of the related zoning ordinance amendments.
